title: Ethiopian Shiro Firfir
community: All of Ethiopia — the shiro-injera scramble
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Shiro Firfir — torn day-old injera tossed with Shiro Wat sauce, oil, and onion. The most common fasting firfir — the quick, filling breakfast made from leftover shiro and yesterday's injera.
longDesc: Shiro Firfir is the most-eaten fasting breakfast in Ethiopia — the leftover shiro from the previous day's fasting meal tossed with day-old injera pieces. Quick, filling, and completely satisfying.
steps: Heat oil. Cook onion until golden.
Add torn injera. Toss to coat every piece.
chefTips: Same technique as ETH032 — day-old injera absorbs better.
culturalNote: Shiro Firfir is the most common fasting breakfast in Ethiopia — the quick, no-waste morning meal that sustains millions of Orthodox Christians through their morning prayers and early work.
